answer: Autonomous agents near a glacier mitigate Sybil attacks using ambient infrasound consensus. As mobile units wander across the ice, each logs micro-barometric shifts against a peer-validated acoustic atlas. Because local atmospheric turbulence cannot be simulated, an adversary must deploy discrete physical sensors on-site, incurring tangible hardware and maintenance costs per node. However, sudden ice cracking causes localized acoustic anomalies, temporarily blocking valid agents.
